blocks.text: Condo buildings in West Chilliwack

The one verified condo building below sits on Evans Road — and current MLS area labels for that same address read "Sardis West Vedder," which shows how loosely the "West Chilliwack" label sits on this ground. Follow the address, not the label.
Cottonwood Village / Cottonwood Mobile Home Park — 7610 Evans Road

This large Evans Road neighbour is a manufactured-home community (listings describe manufactured homes, a 55+ community in central Sardis, and leasehold/park tenure), not a strata apartment-condo building. Do not list it as condo stock.
Other named condo buildings in this sub-area: Not verified
Named condo buildings verified: 1 (Creekside Estates).
Townhomes
Streets, schools and getting around West Chilliwack

items.t: The ground is the western rural/agricultural part of Chilliwack, where the Agricultural Area Plan states the farm sector is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses.

Evans Road is the main local road through the area. BC Transit route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Rd at Yale Rd, Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd and Downtown Chilliwack.
Highway 1 serves the north side of Chilliwack; interchange detail specific to this sub-area is not verified.
The one school physically in the area is Evans Elementary (Kindergarten to Grade 5), 7600 Evans Road.
The Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #104 – 7955 Evans Road, and Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Road.

Where condo stock actually concentrates: it does not concentrate — there is exactly one verified apartment-condo building in the sub-area, on Evans Road. Everything else verified here is freehold farm and rural land under the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in West Chilliwack

items.t: Form B (Strata Property Act, s.59): For Creekside Estates, the Form B is where the monthly fee, any approved levy (ask specifically about roof/deck/window work —'s listing-stated update history), the CRF balance, parking/storage and the insurance summary (required on the Form B since April 1, 2023) are stated.

Rental bylaws void: — long-term rental-restriction bylaws have had no effect since November 24, 2022; short-term rental bylaws remain possible. 55+ bylaws (ss.123.1/123.2) are the only age bylaws permitted, with the May 1, 2023 expanded exemptions for spouses/partners, caregivers and defined children.

Chilliwack zoning: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 governs; the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone that frames most of this sub-area sets a minimum lot area of 7.5 ha for land excluded/exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for an ALC-approved homesite severance, with a 25 m minimum lot width — which is why apartment development is not the form of this area.
Chilliwack OCP: The current city-wide plan is the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500; the Agricultural Area Plan is adopted as a schedule of the OCP.

Floodplain rules that matter even for a condo buyer here: Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets minimum building setbacks of 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal, and the City maintains a diking network for the Fraser and Vedder systems; Chilliwack also levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of municipal rates.

PTT: General 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2M, 3% above, plus 2% on residential value above $3M; first-time buyer exemption on the first $500,000 (max $8,000) up to $835,000, partial to $860,000; Newly Built Home Exemption full to $1,100,000, phasing out at $1,150,000.
HBP $60,000 per person / FHSA $8,000 per year to $40,000 lifetime
CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%: of the mortgage amount; required under 20% down on homes $1.5M or less.
Chilliwack tax dates: property taxes are due the first working day after July 1; for 2026, a 5% penalty applied to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% after August 4, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Chilliwack

items.t: The board boundary is a trap in this sub-area. Anyone quoting a "West Chilliwack median" from that report is quoting nothing.

The Evans Road corridor got a health anchor: the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #104 – 7955 Evans Road is co-located with the Chilliwack and Fraser Health Rural Primary Care Centre, on the same road as the sub-area's only condo building and its elementary school.

Chilliwack's new OCP is recent: the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, is the current city-wide plan, with the Agricultural Area Plan carried as a schedule — the west side's farm-first planning is current policy, not a leftover.

SSMUH arrived unevenly in Chilliwack: Bylaw 5395 (June 18, 2024) implemented it, but the Province's September 16, 2024 extension bulletin gives part of the Proper neighbourhood and Hazel Park until December 31, 2030 to comply — check the specific zone rather than assuming a city-wide rule date.

Drainage and dyking are a separate line on the tax bill in Chilliwack, levied on top of municipal rates — budget for the full notice, not just the municipal rate, whether the purchase is the condo or a farm parcel.

Provincial dates that changed this building's rule book: rental bylaws void November 24, 2022; Form B insurance summary April 1, 2023; 10% CRF minimum November 1, 2023; FVRD depreciation-report catch-up deadline July 1, 2026; FTHB GST rebate in law March 13, 2026 (Bill C-4) for new homes.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in West Chilliwack

Cottonwood Village is a pad-rental park and is not townhouse stock, even though listing form fields say "Townhouse." It is not counted as townhouse inventory. Its placement (West Chilliwack or Sardis West Vedder) is not settled.
Cottonwood Village (Cottonwood Mobile Home Park / Cottonwood Retirement Village) — 7610 Evans Road. Not townhouse stock.

Listings for homes in the park carry form fields that say "Townhouse" and "Row / Townhouse," and listing copy calls units "duplex-style townhouse" and "rancher-style townhome" — and none of that makes it townhouse stock, because the tenure is pad rental: the buyer purchases a manufactured home and rents the pad, on leased land, with "No strata" recorded and a monthly pad fee.
Streets, schools and getting around West Chilliwack

items.t: The residential framing is the western rural and agricultural part of the city, planned through the Agricultural Area Plan (Schedule B1 of the OCP); the farm sector there is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses.

Evans Road is the main local road through the residential side. BC Transit route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Rd at Yale Rd, Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd and Downtown Chilliwack; route 59 Industrial runs peak-period weekday trips between Downtown Chilliwack, Cottonwood Mall and the Lickman Park & Ride.
Highway 1 serves the north side of Chilliwack; interchange configuration detail specific to this sub-area is not verified.

Where townhouse stock actually concentrates: nowhere in this sub-area. Everything verified here is freehold farm and rural land under the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone, plus one apartment-condo building and one manufactured-home park, both on Evans Road and neither of them townhouse stock.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in West Chilliwack

items.t: If it is strata: Form B first: Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance, parking/storage allocations and a summary of the strata's insurance, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. That is the diligence track for Creekside Estates (the sub-area's one strata building) and for any townhouse strata ever built here.

Age bylaws (strata): only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023). Cottonwood Village's 55+ rule is not a strata bylaw — it is a manufactured-home park rule under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act — one more reason it is not townhouse stock.

If it is fee-simple: no strata at all: A fee-simple townhouse carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees — municipal rules (zoning, OCP, floodplain bylaw) plus any registered covenants govern instead. West Chilliwack's rural homes are fee-simple in exactly this sense, but they are detached farm and acreage homes, not townhouse complexes.

Chilliwack zoning: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: The AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone that frames most of this sub-area sets a minimum lot area of 7.5 ha for land excluded/exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for an ALC-approved homesite severance, with a 25 m minimum lot width — which is why townhouse development is not the form of this area.
Chilliwack OCP: Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500: The Agricultural Area Plan is its Schedule B1 and covers this sub-area; the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan is Schedule B5.

Floodplain rules: Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets minimum building setbacks of 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal; the City maintains a diking network for the Fraser and Vedder systems and levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of municipal rates.

items.t: The downgrade and the fresh verification are both stated in rather than silently harmonized.

The board boundary is a trap in this sub-area. The SnapStats reports contain no Chilliwack section at all, because Chilliwack is a different board (CADREB) and is not covered by SnapStats. Anyone quoting a "West Chilliwack median townhouse price" from that source is quoting nothing — and no townhome-only figure exists in any case, because SnapStats splits Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined.

Older plan citations in circulation are out of date. The current plan is Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw No. 5500, with the Agricultural Area Plan as Schedule B1 (this sub-area) and the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan as Schedule B5.
The Sardis West Vedder 55+ complexes are apartment-form, which is why they never surface as townhomes.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in West Chilliwack
The ground in West Chilliwack

items.t: Fee-simple farm and rural parcels: A fee-simple acreage purchase carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fee; municipal/ALR rules and title covenants govern instead.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around West Chilliwack

items.t: Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. The western rural and agricultural ground is planned through the City's Agricultural Area Plan, a schedule of the Official Community Plan; the current city-wide plan is the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500.
Nearby areas: the rest of Chilliwack to the east (downtown, Sardis and the Garrison Crossing side), with Highway 1 serving the north side of the city.
Search names: "West Chilliwack" and the Evans Road corridor name ("Evans," from BC Transit route 52 Evans and Evans Elementary). No other official alternate name was confirmed.

Roads/transit: Evans Road and Lickman Road are the main local corridors. BC Transit route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Rd at Yale Rd, Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd and Downtown Chilliwack; route 59 Industrial runs peak-period trips between Downtown Chilliwack, Cottonwood Mall and the Lickman Park & Ride (weekday trips shown at 6:30 a.m. and 7:30 a.m. toward Cottonwood Mall / Lickman, and 4:10 p.m. and 5:05 p.m. back).

Services are outside the sub-area: nearest recreation centres are Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre (Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street) and Cheam Leisure Centre (45501 Market Way); Chilliwack Library is at 45860 First Avenue; the nearest grocery named by the City is Save-on-Foods, 46020 Yale Road; Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Rd and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #104-7955 Evans Road.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in West Chilliwack

items.t: AL (Agricultural Lowland) — 7.5 ha minimum lot area for land excluded or exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within the ALR; 1 ha for a boundary adjustment; 0.2 ha for an ALC-approved homesite severance or boundary adjustment; 25 m minimum lot width.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Chilliwack

items.t: The Evans Road corridor holds three different tenures within a few doors: "Evans Road acreage" is not one product.

Drainage and dyking are a separate tax line here: Chilliwack levies additional taxes for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rates, and the penalty clock runs twice in a summer — 5% after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 4, 2026.

Route 59 Industrial is peak-only: A handful of weekday trips via the Lickman Park & Ride (6:30 a.m. and 7:30 a.m. out; 4:10 p.m. and 5:05 p.m. back) — do not sell the corridor as transit-served for shift workers without checking the actual timetable. Route 52 Evans is the all-day Evans Road service.

The parks and communities

items.t: Pet rule — conflict carried open: the park specialist's list records 1 pet allowed at Cottonwood Village; an individual listing records 2 smaller pets permitted. unresolved on the sources read — the park rules govern; confirm the current rule with the park before writing an offer around a pet.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around West Chilliwack

items.t: The named corridor is Evans Road: Evans Elementary (K–5) is at 7600 Evans Road, and BC Transit route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and Downtown Chilliwack with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Rd at Yale Rd, Hodgins Ave at Ashwell Rd and Downtown Chilliwack. Highway 1 serves the north side of Chilliwack; interchange detail for this area is not verified.
The farm sector in the plan area is dominated by dairy and poultry operations, nurseries and greenhouses (the City plan's generic sector description — not a confirmation about any named parcel).

Services: the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is inside the corridor at #104 - 7955 Evans Road; Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Rd; the nearest recreation centres (Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, 9145 Corbould Street; Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way) and Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue) are outside the area; the nearest grocery named by the City is Save-on-Foods, 46020 Yale Road.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect park-home buyers in West Chilliwack

items.t: Age rules — sources discipline: In a strata, only a 55+ bylaw is valid (next bullet); a park's 45+ or 40+ marketing number (Country Park Village, Rainbow Estates — not this ground) survives, if at all, only as a park rule under the Human Rights Code 55+ assignment framework, which is written around age 55 — read the actual park rules, not the marketing number.

Chilliwack plan / zoning frame: OCP = Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500 (current); the Agricultural Area Plan is Schedule B1 and covers this sub-area (Sardis = Schedule B5; Agricultural Plan = B1; Eastern Hillsides = B4; Chilliwack Proper = B-2; Downtown = B3 + D-6). Zoning: Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 (s. 6 farm zones); the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone minimums are 7.5 ha (ALR-excluded/exempted or ALC-approved subdivision), 1 ha (boundary adjustment), 0.2 ha (ALC-approved homesite severance), 25 m minimum lot width. SSMUH Bylaw 5395, adopted June 18, 2024 — and SSMUH does not apply to pad tenancies; on ALR ground the ALR rules govern, not SSMUH density (the Province's extension for part of Chilliwack Proper/Hazel Park to December 31, 2030 is not this sub-area).

ALR BLOCK IN FULL (this sub-area is farm ground throughout): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within the principal residence only, additional residence 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 + 5% of the farm operation's value over 4 ha, $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by October 31. Parcel-level ALR status is per address on ALC mapping — not verified for any parcel here until checked. Floodplain: Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 setbacks — 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River, 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal — with City diking for the Fraser/Vedder systems and drainage/dyking levies on top of municipal rates.

blocks.text: Good to know about West Chilliwack

items.t: The two Evans Road addresses side by side are opposite products: Neither is a townhouse complex, and search results that blur the corridor blur the tenure.

The lease clock is the real due-diligence item at Cottonwood: Three listing positions (2076 + extension option / November 30, 2039 / ~16 years, with a side conflict over whether the land is First Nations leasehold and one "cash purchase only" note) mean the head-lease summary and park rules must be in hand before subject removal — a lender, an insurer and the next buyer will all price the remaining term.
The Bylaw 3055 conflict is open in the City's own materials: The City's subdivisions webpage names a "Land Development Bylaw 2014, No. 3055"; the verified ledger holds it was never adopted.
Outdated plan citations are common on this ground. Current: Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw 5500, with the Agricultural Plan as Schedule B1 (this ground) and Sardis as B5.

Dyking is a line item, not an abstraction: Chilliwack levies drainage and dyking taxes on top of municipal rates and maintains the Fraser/Vedder diking network — a holding-cost fact that never appears in a listing's tax summary, for a park home's tax bill as much as a farm parcel's.

faq.a: One verified: Creekside Estates, 7694 Evans Road (strata plan LMS1320, built 1993). The large complex next door at 7610 Evans Road is a manufactured-home park, not condos.
faq.q: How many condo buildings are there in West Chilliwack?

faq.a: The answer for a specific unit is in the Form B and the strata's current budget — ask for both, plus the depreciation report, before subject removal.
faq.q: What do strata fees at Creekside Estates cover?

faq.a: Treat that as a prompt to verify the full project history and what remains in the depreciation report, not as a building guarantee.
faq.q: Has the building had big capital work?

faq.a: Long-term: yes in law — rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be banned by bylaw; check the filed bylaws.
faq.q: Can I rent out a unit at Creekside Estates?

faq.a: Listings for units in the building record carport parking and in-suite laundry; the specific stall (and any locker) assigned to a unit is stated on the Form B — confirm it there rather than from a listing.
The attached-looking product on Evans Road is one apartment-condo building (Creekside Estates) and one manufactured-home park (Cottonwood Village).
faq.q: Are there any townhouses in West Chilliwack?

faq.a: In form-field language only. The home is a manufactured home on a rented pad on leased land, with no strata — you do not own the land, there is no Form B, and the tenancy runs under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act.
faq.q: A listing calls a Cottonwood Village home a townhouse. Is it one?

faq.a: An individual fee-simple farm or rural parcel — land bought as farm land with a homesite, in a working agricultural landscape under the AL zone and the Agricultural Area Plan (Schedule B1). There is no acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product to buy instead.
faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy an "acreage" in West Chilliwack?

faq.a: The City floodplain bylaw requires buildings to sit at least 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal — measure them before valuing the buildable area of any lot near a river or canal.
faq.q: What flood setbacks apply to a rural lot?

faq.a: SD33 catchments are address-based. Any other address needs its own locator run.
faq.q: Which schools serve a West Chilliwack acreage?

faq.a: Its sub-area placement (West Chilliwack vs Sardis West Vedder) and its head-lease terms are both unresolved conflicts — search both sub-area names and diligence the lease, not the label.
faq.q: What can I actually buy in West Chilliwack if I want a mobile/manufactured home?

faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — that is not land ownership — and the park itself sits on leased land under a head lease. There is no strata, no Form B, and the tenancy runs under the MHPTA plus the park rules and the head lease.
faq.q: Do I own the land at Cottonwood Village?

faq.a: unresolved. Listings state 2076 with an option to extend, November 30, 2039, and ~16 years remaining — and they even conflict on whether the land is First Nations leasehold. The head lease and pad tenancy agreement answer it; listing copy does not, and lenders/insurers will ask the same question.
faq.q: How long is the Cottonwood lease, really?

faq.a: Once every 12 months, on at least 3 full months' notice, by inflation plus the park's proportional levy/utility amount: 2.3% + proportional for 2026, 2.2% + proportional for 2027 (RTB, verified Nov 1, 2026).
faq.q: How much can my pad rent go up?

faq.a: Only through the Approving Officer / PLA process, with ALC approval inside the ALR, and only if the AL zone minimums are met (7.5 ha, or 0.2 ha for an ALC-approved homesite severance; 25 m minimum width).
faq.q: Can I subdivide a West Chilliwack parcel into half-duplex lots?

faq.a: The floodplain bylaw requires at least 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal — measure the setback on the specific lot before pricing in a build.
faq.q: How close to a river can I build?

faq.a: Drainage and dyking levies sit on top of the municipal rates — read the full notice, not just the municipal line — and the 2026 penalties run 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after August 4.
faq.q: What extra holding costs hide in the tax notice?
